Why Termite Inspections Are Critical

Termites work silently. By the time you notice damage, thousands of dollars in structural repairs are already needed. A professional inspection detects termites before they become catastrophic.

Structural Damage

Can cost $25,000+ to repair. Early detection saves thousands.

Home Value

Termite history can reduce home resale value 10-20%.

Insurance Issues

Most homeowners insurance doesn't cover termite damage.

Hidden Damage

Termites hide inside walls. You need professionals to find them.

7 Signs You May Have Termites

Many of these signs are invisible. That's why professional inspection is critical.

Mud Tubes

HIGH RISK

Thin mud-like tunnels on walls, crawlspaces, or foundations. Termites use these for protection.

Wood Damage

CRITICAL

Hollow-sounding wood, blistering paint, or visible damage to framing and walls.

Swarmers

IMMEDIATE

Winged termites during spring (April-May). Often mistaken for flying ants. This means active infestation.

Discarded Wings

HIGH RISK

After swarming season, you may find piles of wings on windowsills or near lights.

Frass (Termite Droppings)

HIGH RISK

Small, dark pellets that look like sawdust or sand. Found near termite activity.

Sagging Floors

CRITICAL

Structural settling or bouncy floors indicate damage to support beams. This is serious.

Clicking Sounds

MEDIUM

Soldier termites make clicking sounds when disturbed. Audible from inside walls.

NO VISIBLE SIGNS

SNEAKY

The most dangerous scenario. Termites can work undetected for 3-8 years. Professional inspection is ONLY way to know.

Seeing any of these signs? Don't wait. Termites cause exponential damage the longer they feed.

Our Professional Inspection Process

1

Initial Assessment

We walk your property, identify potential entry points, and assess risk factors (moisture, wood-to-soil contact, age of home).

2

Detailed Inspection

Licensed termite inspectors examine crawlspace, attic, foundation, exterior, and interior walls. We use moisture meters and acoustic listening devices.

3

Attic & Crawlspace Inspection

The most common areas for termite damage. We look for mud tubes, damaged wood, frass, and termite activity.

4

Foundation & Perimeter Check

Inspect foundation cracks, soil-to-wood contact, gutters/drainage, and exterior wood damage.

5

Written Report

Detailed findings with photos, risk assessment, and treatment recommendations if needed.

6

Treatment Plan (If Needed)

If termites detected, we explain treatment options: barriers, spot treatments, bait systems, or monitoring.

Treatment Options (If Termites Found)

We'll explain all options and recommend the best solution for your situation.

Liquid Barriers

Protective chemicals applied to soil around foundation. Creates barrier termites cannot cross.

Effectiveness:

Highly effective

Duration:

3-5 years

Bait Systems

Tamper-proof stations placed around property. Termites consume poison and carry it back to colony (slow kill).

Effectiveness:

Extremely effective

Duration:

Ongoing monitoring

Spot Treatments

For isolated infestations inside walls. Injection into damaged wood areas.

Effectiveness:

Targeted solution

Duration:

As needed
